text:
Minutes of the staff meeting of Companion Animal Travel Desk at Aurelia Skyways were recorded for internal safety review. Attendees were Diego Wilson, Noah Wong, and Winnie.

The chair opened by restating that each journey must be handled as a shared responsibility, with the welfare coordinator reviewing comfort needs before any transfer is approved. Staff were reminded that the transfer path must remain controlled, documented, and limited to the steps already cleared for the case. <<FACT F106>> The team agreed that any escalation must be handled without delay and only through the approved channel, with attention to animal welfare and passenger calm.

Attention then turned to check-in oversight. The group confirmed that the check-in process must remain closely supervised so that carriers, labels, and handoff details are checked before movement begins. <<FACT F098>> It was noted that early review reduces the risk of confusion at the service point and helps the staff keep a consistent record for each animal. The meeting emphasized that the person overseeing check-in must verify comfort indicators, confirm identity details, and note any special handling request in plain terms.

Discussion also covered communication between the desk and the flight-side team. Staff were instructed to use simple language, avoid informal promises, and document every instruction that affects the animal's route. The welfare coordinator advised that changes in behavior, temperature sensitivity, or signs of distress must be reported at once, since the desk is responsible for protecting the animal from unnecessary stress. The team also reviewed the need to keep the owner informed without adding uncertainty, especially when the animal may be sensitive to noise or separation.

The staff agreed that service consistency depends on careful handover discipline. Records must be complete before any transfer is advanced, and no step should be skipped to save time. The chair reminded the team that the safety standard applies equally to routine and complex cases, and that a calm process helps the animal settle. The meeting concluded with agreement that future reviews will focus on clearer logging, prompt escalation where needed, and steady coordination across the desk.
